sections.heading: Someone Who Tells You What the Roof Needs
body: A roof is a big job to hand to people you've never met, and most homeowners only do it once or twice.

It goes wrong when a salesperson promises one thing and the crew that shows up never heard it. At Monarch, Cesar is the one who looks at your roof, explains the work and checks in with you while the job is going.
He also tells you what the roof actually needs. Sometimes that's a new roof. Sometimes it's a few repairs, and we'd rather say so than sell you a roof you don't need.

sections.heading: Roof Replacement
body: Most people call about a replacement after putting it off. Shingles curl at the edges, bare spots show where the granules have worn away, and a stain appears on a ceiling after the first hard rain.
Asphalt shingles wear out slowly and then quickly. Once they go brittle, patching one spot just moves the leak to the next weak one.
Cesar looks at the roof, explains the process and the materials, and gives you the price. Then our crew does the work, and many houses are finished in a day.

sections.quote: I had put off getting my roof replaced for the longest time because I didn’t want to hassle with it and the process. Caesar made the process very easy, they were out here within the week getting my roof done and did an excellent job!
sections.name: Kayla H.

sections.heading: Roof Repair
body: A few shingles in the yard after a windy night, or a drip over the dining room, does not always mean a new roof.

Water travels. It runs along the deck and drops somewhere far from where it got in, so the stain on your ceiling is rarely under the problem. We find where the water is really coming in, fix that, and tell you honestly if the rest of the roof has years left.

sections.heading: When Hail or Wind Hits
body: After a Kansas storm, the roof often looks fine from the driveway. Hail bruises shingles and loosens their granules, and the damage shows up months later as a leak.

If your insurance company is involved, the adjuster's visit is the moment the damage gets written down. We look at your roof first, tell you plainly whether there's damage, and go to the adjuster's inspection.

We talk with your insurance company for you and send the paperwork in. What an insurer pays is their decision, and nobody honest can promise it. Our part is showing the adjuster the damage we found on your roof.

sections.quote: Once I agreed to Cesar inspecting my roof after a hail storm, which he verified, he took care of everything else, including being on-site during the insurance adjuster's inspection. Cesar and Monarch Roofing made the entire process unbelievably easy and really earned my trust.
sections.name: Jim W.

sections.heading: When You Have a Closing Date
body: A buyer's inspector looks at the roof, and an old one can hold up a sale. If you're selling, a roof that's near the end of its life is better dealt with before you list than after an offer.
Tell us the date when you call. We plan the job around it.

sections.quote: They were efficient, stayed on schedule, and got our roof replaced in time for us to list our home.

sections.heading: Gutters and Siding
body: Gutters and the roof edge are one system. Hail that dents a gutter has usually hit the shingles above it, so we look at both at once.
That's why we put new gutters on in the same job as a new roof when they need it. You get one schedule, and the roof edge and gutters are finished together.
We also do siding, as part of a roof job or as a project of its own.

sections.heading: How You Know It's Time
body: Most asphalt shingle roofs last somewhere between 20 and 30 years, less where hail and hot summers are hard on them. The signs are usually easy to spot once you know to look.
Shingles curl or crack. Bare patches show where the granules have worn off. The gutters fill with grit, a ceiling stains after rain, or shingles keep blowing into the yard.
One of those isn't always the end of the roof. If it's one slope or a few shingles, [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/) may be all you need. Cesar will tell you which it is.

Cesar inspects the roof first and tells you whether there's damage. He goes to the adjuster's inspection, talks with your insurance company, and we send in the paperwork.
We can't tell you what an insurer will pay, and nobody honest can. Our part is showing the adjuster the damage we found.

sections.heading: Choosing Your Shingles
body: The shingle you pick changes how long the roof lasts. A basic three-tab shingle is the cheapest and the thinnest. Architectural shingles are thicker, hold up longer and look better.

In hail country there's a third option: Class 4 impact-resistant shingles, made to pass the toughest impact test shingles are rated on. They cost more than standard shingles, and we've installed them.
Cesar walks you through the choices and the cost of each, and you pick the color you can live with.

body: Gutters sit right under the roof edge, so they get hit by the same hail and wear out on the same schedule. Putting new gutters on after a new roof means paying a crew to come out twice.
When yours need replacing, we do both in the same job. You get a single schedule, and the roof edge and gutters are done together.

sections.heading: What a Good Replacement Includes
body: Whoever you hire, a replacement done right has these parts. Ask any roofer to confirm each one before you sign.
list: The old roofing comes off down to the deck, so the wood underneath can be checked.
Soft or rotted decking is replaced, not covered over.
New underlayment goes down, along with flashing at the chimneys, walls and vents.
Ventilation in the attic is checked, because a hot attic cooks shingles from below.
New shingles are nailed in the pattern the manufacturer calls for.

sections.heading: Why It Matters What's Under the Shingles
body: Most roof failures start in the details, not in the shingles. A leak at a chimney is usually flashing, and a roof that ages early is often an attic that can't breathe.
That's why we want to look at the whole roof before we price it.

sections.heading: Install Day
body: Our crew starts early. Many houses are finished in a day, and we've done bigger ones in a day too.
Larger or more complicated roofs, and any rotted decking found under the old shingles, can add time.
If you have a closing date, give it to us when you call. We plan the job around it.

sections.quote: The roofers came in early just before I went in for work and were done by the time I got home!! Everything was cleaned up and the roof looked incredible.

Then we walk the finished roof with you, so you see what was done before we leave.

sections.heading: Shingles Blown Off in the Wind
body: You find them in the grass after a windy night, or you see a bare strip on the roof from the street.
Shingles hold down with a sealant strip and a few nails. When the strip dries out and lets go, the wind gets under the edge and pulls the shingle up. The next gust takes the one beside it.
A repair puts new shingles in and seals the ones around them. It's worth doing quickly, because bare felt and exposed nails let water into the deck.

image.alt: Shingle roof slope with a few shingles newly replaced after wind
image.brief: shingle roof slope with a small section of newer shingles, roof on the right, open sky on the left behind the text side, no readable text, no people, no tools

sections.heading: A Leak Isn't Always Where the Stain Is
body: Water doesn't drip straight down. It runs along the roof deck and the rafters until it finds a gap in the ceiling, so the stain can be many feet from the hole.
That's why guessing at a leak gets expensive. Patch the wrong spot and the stain comes back the next time it rains.
Cesar looks for where the water gets in, not where it shows up. That means checking the roof surface, the flashing and the attic side when it matters.

sections.quote: I had Cesar with Monarch Roofing come out to a project to help identify a water leak. I only had to give him a brief overview of the issue, and he immediately pinpointed the problem. … Cesar was quick to get his crew scheduled, and they completed the work in a timely and professional manner.
sections.name: Francisco T.

sections.heading: Where Roofs Usually Leak
body: Most leaks aren't in the middle of a shingle field. They start at the places where the roof changes direction or something goes through it.
list: Flashing around chimneys, skylights and the walls where a lower roof meets a higher one.
Plumbing vents and roof vents, where the rubber collar cracks in the sun.
Valleys, where two slopes meet and carry the most water.
Nail heads that have worked loose and lifted a shingle.
Hail or wind damage that has opened the shingle surface.

sections.heading: Why Repairs Fail
body: Most repairs that come back were fixing the stain. A dab of sealant on the wrong spot hides the problem until the next rain.
A repair that lasts replaces the failed part: the flashing, the collar or the damaged shingles, not the symptom. If you've patched the same spot twice, the real problem is somewhere else.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace? We'll Tell You Which
body: Repair makes sense when the damage is limited and the rest of the roof is sound. A few missing shingles, one bad flashing and one failed vent are all repairs.
Replacement makes sense when shingles are cracking across the whole roof, granules are gone from every slope, or the same leak keeps coming back.
We'd rather give you the honest answer than the bigger job. If you've been told you need a whole roof and you're not sure, call and have Cesar look before you sign.

sections.quote: The team is knowledgeable, professional, and takes the time to explain the entire process clearly. They’re honest, reliable, and truly care about delivering quality work.
sections.name: Rosario V.

sections.heading: What a Repair Visit Looks Like
body: Cesar comes out, looks at the roof and finds the source. He explains what he found and what it will take to fix it.
Then he schedules the crew, and you know the price before they start. If the roof turns out to be past repairing, he tells you that, and why.

sections.heading: Repairs After a Storm
body: If hail or wind caused the damage, take photos before anyone patches it. The adjuster needs to see what happened, and a patched roof can hide it.

A small repair and a hail claim are separate jobs. A few lifted shingles is a repair. Hail damage across the roof can be a replacement, and that decision is worth making before you spend money on patches.
If your insurance company is involved, we inspect the roof, go to the adjuster's inspection and talk with them for you. See [roof replacement](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/) for how that goes.

items.q: How much does a roof repair cost?
items.a: It depends on what has failed and how much roof is involved. A cracked vent collar or a few blown-off shingles is a small job; re-flashing a chimney or rebuilding a valley is a bigger one. Cesar looks at it and gives you a price before the work starts.

items.q: How soon can you get here?
items.a: Call (316) 223-3575, Monday to Saturday, 8 AM to 6 PM, and we'll set a time for Cesar to look. If water is coming in now, say so on the call so we know it can't wait.

items.q: Can you tell me over the phone if I need a new roof?
items.a: Not honestly. A stain, a missing shingle and a hail dent can look the same from a description and be very different on the roof.

items.q: What should I do until the roof is fixed?
items.a: Move things out from under the leak, catch the drip and take photos of the stain and any damage. Don't climb on a wet roof.
